translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The upadhi (adjunct) comes and goes; it is the same Self that acts and enjoys; it is the same Self that decays and dies. But I, ever unchanged, am established like a mountain, immovable.

text: न मे प्रवृत्तिर्न च मे निवृत्तिः सदैकरूपस्य निरंशकस्य । एकात्मको यो निविडो निरन्तरो व्योमेव पूर्णः स कथं नु चेष्टते ॥ ५०२ ॥

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Neither action nor inaction belongs to me, who am ever one in nature, without parts, who am singular, dense, unbroken, and full like space—how could such a one possibly act?

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: मुझे न तो प्रवृत्ति है और न ही निवृत्ति, जो मैं सदा एकरूप, अंशहीन, एकात्मक, निरन्तर और आकाश की तरह पूर्ण हूँ—ऐसा कोई कैसे क्रिया कर सकता है?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: For one who is devoid of senses, without mind, unchanging, and unconditioned, where can merit and demerit belong? How can the Sruti say that even this (merit and demerit) does not come near me, who experience the indivisible bliss?

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: जिसके पास इन्द्रियें नहीं हैं, मन नहीं है, अपरिवर्तनशील है और असंयुक्त है, उसके लिए पुण्य और पाप कहाँ हो सकते हैं? श्रुति कैसे कह सकती है कि यह (पुण्य और पाप) मेरे पास नहीं आते, जो अखण्ड सुख का अनुभव करता हूँ?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the sun is merely a witness to actions, just as fire is the mere enabler of burning, and just as the rope has no real connection with the imagined snake—so too, O my Self, the immutable Consciousness (Kutastha) has no real association with the superimposed phenomena.

transliteration: kartāpi vā kārayitāpi nāhaṃ bhoktāpi vā bhojayitāpi nāham | draṣṭāpi vā darśayitāpi nāhaṃ so'haṃ svayaṃjyotiranīdṛgātmā || 507 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am neither the doer nor the one who causes others to act; I am neither the enjoyer nor the one who causes others to enjoy; I am neither the seer nor the one who causes others to see. I am that very Self, the self-luminous, unchanging, and non-dual Consciousness.

translations.text: मैं न तो कर्ता हूँ और न ही कार्य करवाने वाला; मैं न तो भोक्ता हूँ और न ही भोजन करवाने वाला; मैं न तो द्रष्टा हूँ और न ही दर्शन करवाने वाला। मैं वही स्वयंज्योति, अनीदृश, अखंड आत्मा हूँ।

sanskrit_shloka: चलत्युपाधौ प्रतिबिम्बलौल्यम् अउपाधिकं मूढधियो नयन्ति । स्वबिम्बभूतं रविवद्विनिष्क्रियं कर्तास्मि भोक्तास्मि हतोऽस्मि हेति ॥ ५०८ ॥
text: चलत्युपाधौ प्रतिबिम्बलौल्यम् अउपाधिकं मूढधियो नयन्ति । स्वबिम्बभूतं रविवद्विनिष्क्रियं कर्तास्मि भोक्तास्मि हतोऽस्मि हेति ॥ ५०८ ॥
transliteration: calatyupādhau pratibimbalaulyam aupādhikaṃ mūḍhadhiyo nayanti | svabimbabhūtaṃ ravivadviniṣkriyaṃ kartāsmi bhoktāsmi hato'smi heti || 508 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The reflection's movement appears in the upadhi; the deluded mind attributes this to the reflection's source, which is itself motionless like the sun. Thus, the ignorant say, 'I am the doer,' 'I am the enjoyer,' 'I am destroyed.'

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: उपाधि में प्रतिबिम्ब की गति दिखाई देती है; मूढ़ बुद्धि इसे प्रतिबिम्ब के स्रोत, जो सूर्य की तरह निष्क्रिय है, को देती है। अतः अज्ञानी कहते हैं, 'मैं कर्ता हूँ,' 'मैं भोक्ता हूँ,' 'मैं नष्ट हो गया हूँ।'

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Whether rolling in water or on land, the inert body may be subject to such qualities; but I am not stained by those attributes, just as space is not stained by the qualities of the pot.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Attributes such as doership, enjoyership, wickedness, delusion, inertness, bondage, and liberation are mere modifications of the intellect; they do not truly exist in the Self, which is the supreme, solitary, non-dual Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Let the modifications of Prakriti be tenfold, a hundredfold, a thousandfold, or more—what does it matter to me, the unattached witness? Just as the dense sky never touches the clouds, so too does the Self remain untouched by them.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This universe, extending from the unmanifest to the gross, is perceived merely as an appearance; that Brahman, non-dual, subtle like space, without beginning or end—verily, I am that.

translations.text: That Brahman, non-dual, which is the essence of pure existence, knowledge, and bliss, beyond all distinctions of Maya, directly experienced as the innermost Self, known by the inner awareness — that very Brahman am I.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This sovereignty and imperial majesty, this supreme glory, has been attained by me through the grace, splendor, and benevolence of my revered Guru, the great soul. Salutations to you, again and again, salutations!

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: O Guru, with utmost compassion, awaken this one who wanders, tormented day after day in the great dream of Maya, entangled in the dense thicket of birth, old age, and death, and grievously wounded by the tiger of egoism—awaken him from this slumber and make him realize the Supreme Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: One who constantly perceives Brahman as the sole reality of the world, with the inner vision and a tranquil mind, sees Brahman in all conditions. What else, besides Brahman, can be perceived by those whose eyes are awakened? translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The food is that which is free from thought and obtained without begging; the drink is water from rivers; the posture is free and unbound; sleep is fearless in the cremation ground or forest; the garment is free from washing, drying, and similar rituals; the dwelling is the directions; the bed is the earth; the movement is in the paths of the Vedic conclusions; and the sport of the wise is in the Supreme Brahman.

translations.text: भोजन वह है जो चिंतारहित है और भिक्षा के बिना प्राप्त होता है; पानी नदियों का जल है; स्थिति स्वतंत्र और अनाबद्ध है; निद्रा कब्रिस्तान या वन में निर्भय है; वस्त्र धोने, सूखने आदि के बिना है; निवास सभी दिशाएँ हैं; शय्या पृथ्वी है; यात्रा वेदान्त के मार्गों में है; और विद्वानों का खेल परम ब्रह्म में है।

sanskrit_shloka: विमानमालम्ब्य शरीरमेतद् भुनक्त्यशेषान्विषयानुपस्थितान् । परेच्छया बालवदात्मवेत्ता योऽव्यक्तलिङ्गोऽननुषक्तबाह्यः ॥ ५३९ ॥
text: विमानमालम्ब्य शरीरमेतद् भुनक्त्यशेषान्विषयानुपस्थितान् । परेच्छया बालवदात्मवेत्ता योऽव्यक्तलिङ्गोऽननुषक्तबाह्यः ॥ ५३९ ॥
transliteration: vimānamālambya śarīrametad bhunaktyaśeṣānviṣayānupasthitān | parecchayā bālavadātmavettā yo'vyaktaliṅgo'nanuṣaktabāhyaḥ || 539 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Having seized the body as a vehicle, the Self-knower, like a child, enjoys all sense objects that are not yet manifest, guided by the will of another; he is unattached to external objects and has an unmanifest subtle body.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: शरीर को एक वाहन के रूप में ग्रहण करके, आत्मज्ञानी, एक बालक की तरह, अभी तक प्रकट न हुए सभी विषयों का भोग करता है, अन्य की इच्छा से चलकर; वह बाह्य विषयों से अनुलग्न नहीं है और उसका सूक्ष्म शरीर अव्यक्त है।

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Whether he is sky-clad, clothed in garments, clothed in skin, or established in pure consciousness, whether he behaves like a madman, a child, or a ghost—he wanders in the world.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: चाहे वह आकाश का वस्त्र धारण करे, वस्त्र धारण करे, त्वचा धारण करे, या शुद्ध चैतन्य में स्थित हो; चाहे वह पागल की तरह, बच्चे की तरह या पिशाच की तरह व्यवहार करे—वह इस संसार में भटकता रहता है।

text: कामान्निष्कामरूपी संश्चरत्येकचारो मुनिः । स्वात्मनैव सदा तुष्टः स्वयं सर्वात्मना स्थितः ॥ ५४१ ॥
transliteration: kāmānniṣkāmarūpī saṃścaratyekacāro muniḥ | svātmanaiva sadā tuṣṭaḥ svayaṃ sarvātmanā sthitaḥ || 541 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The sage, who is desireless even while appearing to engage in desires, wanders alone, ever content in the Self alone, established in the All-Self.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: वह मुनि, जो कामों के साथ व्यवहार करते हुए भी निष्काम है, एकाकी घूमता है, सदैव अपने ही आत्मा में संतुष्ट और सर्वात्मा में स्थित।

sanskrit_shloka: क्वचिन्मूढो विद्वान् क्वचिदपि महाराजविभवः क्वचिद्भ्रान्तः सौम्यः क्वचिदजगराचारकलितः । क्वचित्पात्रीभूतः क्वचिदवमतः क्वाप्यविदितः चरत्येवं प्राज्ञः सततपरमानन्दसुखितः ॥ ५४२ ॥
text: क्वचिन्मूढो विद्वान् क्वचिदपि महाराजविभवः क्वचिद्भ्रान्तः सौम्यः क्वचिदजगराचारकलितः । क्वचित्पात्रीभूतः क्वचिदवमतः क्वाप्यविदितः चरत्येवं प्राज्ञः सततपरमानन्दसुखितः ॥ ५४२ ॥
transliteration: kvacinmūḍho vidvān kvacidapi mahārājavibhavaḥ kvacidbhrāntaḥ saumyaḥ kvacidajagarācārakalitaḥ | kvacitpātrībhūtaḥ kvacidavamataḥ kvāpyaviditaḥ caratyevaṃ prājñaḥ satataparamānandasukhitaḥ || 542 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Sometimes the wise one appears foolish, sometimes he possesses royal splendor; sometimes he seems deluded, yet gentle; sometimes he behaves like a serpent; sometimes he is honored, sometimes disrespected, and sometimes unknown. Thus moves the wise one, ever enjoying supreme bliss.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: कभी विद्वान् मूढ़ लगता है, कभी वह महाराज की शोभा धारण करता है; कभी वह भ्रान्त लगता है, पर सौम्य; कभी वह साँप की तरह व्यवहार करता है; कभी वह सम्मानित होता है, कभी अवमानित, और कभी अज्ञात। इस प्रकार वह प्राज्ञ चलता है, सदैव परमानन्द का आनन्द भोग करता हुआ।

sanskrit_shloka: निर्धनोऽपि सदा तुष्टोऽप्यसहायो महाबलः । नित्यतृप्तोऽप्यभुञ्जानोऽप्यसमः समदर्शनः ॥ ५४३ ॥
text: निर्धनोऽपि सदा तुष्टोऽप्यसहायो महाबलः । नित्यतृप्तोऽप्यभुञ्जानोऽप्यसमः समदर्शनः ॥ ५४३ ॥
transliteration: nirdhano'pi sadā tuṣṭo'pyasahāyo mahābalaḥ | nityatṛpto'pyabhuñjāno'pyasamaḥ samadarśanaḥ || 543 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Though destitute, he is always content; though without support, he is mighty; though enjoying nothing, he is eternally satisfied; though unequal, he sees all equally.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: हालांकि निर्धन है, वह सदैव संतुष्ट है; हालांकि बिना सहायता के है, वह महाबली है; हालांकि कुछ भी भोग नहीं करता, वह सदैव परिपूर्ण है; हालांकि असमान है, वह सबको समान देखता है।

sanskrit_shloka: अपि कुर्वन्नकुर्वाणश्चाभोक्ता फलभोग्यपि । शरीर्यप्यशरीर्येष परिच्छिन्नोऽपि सर्वगः ॥ ५४४ ॥
text: अपि कुर्वन्नकुर्वाणश्चाभोक्ता फलभोग्यपि । शरीर्यप्यशरीर्येष परिच्छिन्नोऽपि सर्वगः ॥ ५४४ ॥
transliteration: api kurvannakurvāṇaścābhoktā phalabhogyapi | śarīryapyaśarīryeṣa paricchinno'pi sarvagaḥ || 544 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Though acting or not acting, he is the non-enjoyer even of the fruits of action; though embodied, he is the disembodied; though seemingly limited, he is omnipresent.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: चाहे कर्म करे या न करे, वह कर्म के फलों का भोक्ता नहीं है; चाहे शरीरवान् हो या न हो, वह अशरीरी है; चाहे सीमित प्रतीत हो या न हो, वह सर्वव्यापी है।

transliteration: aśarīraṃ sadā santamimaṃ brahmavidaṃ kvacit | priyāpriye na spṛśatastathaiva ca śubhāśubhe || 545 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This knower of Brahman, who is ever bodiless and real, is never touched by pleasure or pain, nor by the auspicious or inauspicious.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: यह ब्रह्मज्ञ, जो सदैव शरीरहीन और सत्य है, सुख या दुःख, शुभ या अशुभ से कभी स्पर्श नहीं होता।

sanskrit_shloka: स्थूलादिसंबन्धवतोऽभिमानिनः सुखं च दुःखं च शुभाशुभे च । विध्वस्तबन्धस्य सदात्मनो मुनेः कुतः शुभं वाप्यशुभं फलं वा ॥ ५४६ ॥
text: स्थूलादिसंबन्धवतोऽभिमानिनः सुखं च दुःखं च शुभाशुभे च । विध्वस्तबन्धस्य सदात्मनो मुनेः कुतः शुभं वाप्यशुभं फलं वा ॥ ५४६ ॥

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: For one who identifies with gross and other adjuncts, there is pleasure and pain, and auspicious and inauspicious results; but for the sage whose bonds are destroyed and who is ever the Self, whence could arise auspicious or inauspicious fruit?

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: जो ग्रोस और अन्य उपाधियों से अहंकार करता है, उसके लिए सुख और दुःख, शुभ और अशुभ फल होते हैं; परंतु जिस मुनि के बंधन विनष्ट हो चुके हैं और जो सदा आत्मा है, उसके लिए शुभ या अशुभ फल कहाँ से उत्पन्न हो सकता है?

sanskrit_shloka: तमसा ग्रस्तवद्भानादग्रस्तोऽपि रविर्जनैः । ग्रस्त इत्युच्यते भ्रान्त्यां ह्यज्ञात्वा वस्तुलक्षणम् ॥ ५४७ ॥
text: तमसा ग्रस्तवद्भानादग्रस्तोऽपि रविर्जनैः । ग्रस्त इत्युच्यते भ्रान्त्यां ह्यज्ञात्वा वस्तुलक्षणम् ॥ ५४७ ॥
transliteration: tamasā grastavadbhānādagrasto'pi ravirjanaiḥ | grasta ityucyate bhrāntyāṃ hyajñātvā vastulakṣaṇam || 547 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the sun, though not actually swallowed, is said to be swallowed by Rahu during an eclipse due to ignorance of its true nature, so too is the Self perceived as bound by ignorance, though it is never truly obscured.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: जिस प्रकार सूर्य, हालाँकि वास्तव में ग्रस्त नहीं होता, अज्ञानवश राहु द्वारा ग्रस्त कहलाता है, उसी प्रकार आत्मा भी अज्ञानवश बंधित प्रतीत होती है, हालाँकि वह कभी वास्तव में आच्छादित नहीं होती।

sanskrit_shloka: तद्वद्देहादिबन्धेभ्यो विमुक्तं ब्रह्मवित्तमम् । पश्यन्ति देहिवन्मूढाः शरीराभासदर्शनात् ॥ ५४८ ॥
text: तद्वद्देहादिबन्धेभ्यो विमुक्तं ब्रह्मवित्तमम् । पश्यन्ति देहिवन्मूढाः शरीराभासदर्शनात् ॥ ५४८ ॥
transliteration: tadvaddehādibandhebhyo vimuktaṃ brahmavittamam | paśyanti dehivanmūḍhāḥ śarīrābhāsadarśanāt || 548 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the sun is free from the bindings of the earth and its surroundings, so too is the knower of Brahman liberated from the bonds of the body and the like; yet the deluded, identifying themselves with the body, see only the reflection of the body.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: जिस प्रकार सूर्य पृथ्वी और उसके आसपास के बंधनों से मुक्त है, उसी प्रकार ब्रह्मज्ञ शरीर आदि के बंधनों से मुक्त है; किन्तु मूढ़ लोग, जो शरीर के साथ अपनी पहचान करते हैं, केवल शरीर के प्रतिबिंब को ही देखते हैं।

sanskrit_shloka: अहिर्निर्ल्वयनीं वायं मुक्त्वा देहं तु तिष्ठति । इतस्ततश्चाल्यमानो यत्किंचित्प्राणवायुना ॥ ५४९ ॥
text: अहिर्निर्ल्वयनीं वायं मुक्त्वा देहं तु तिष्ठति । इतस्ततश्चाल्यमानो यत्किंचित्प्राणवायुना ॥ ५४९ ॥
transliteration: ahirnirlvayanīṃ vāyaṃ muktvā dehaṃ tu tiṣṭhati | itastataścālyamāno yatkiṃcitprāṇavāyunā || 549 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The serpent, having cast off its old skin, remains; similarly, the Self, having abandoned the body, remains, moving about wherever the vital air carries it.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: साँप अपनी पुरानी त्वचा छोड़कर रह जाता है; इसी प्रकार, आत्मा शरीर को छोड़कर रह जाती है, जहाँ प्राणवायु इसे ले जाता है, वहाँ घूमती रहती है।

sanskrit_shloka: स्त्रोतसा नीयते दारु यथा निम्नोन्नतस्थलम् । दैवेन नीयते देहो यथाकालोपभुक्तिषु ॥ ५५० ॥
text: स्त्रोतसा नीयते दारु यथा निम्नोन्नतस्थलम् । दैवेन नीयते देहो यथाकालोपभुक्तिषु ॥ ५५० ॥
transliteration: strotasā nīyate dāru yathā nimnonnatasthalam | daivena nīyate deho yathākālopabhuktiṣu || 550 ||

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as wood is carried along by the current of a river, moving over low and high places, so the body is carried along by destiny, according to the fruits of past actions to be enjoyed.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: जिस प्रकार नदी के प्रवाह से लकड़ी नीचे और ऊपर के स्थानों पर ले जाई जाती है, उसी प्रकार शरीर भी दैव द्वारा, भोग्य पूर्व कर्मों के अनुसार ले जाया जाता है।
